Ballad

/BAL-uhd/ - rhymes with salad · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Ballad means a slow, sentimental song that tells a story, often of love.

Halfway through the set, the fiddler traded her reels for a ballad about a soldier writing home from the border.

Worked Example

The jukebox at the diner holds one battered 45 the regulars guard: a ballad in which a trucker phones his daughter from every state line, and the final verse ends the call at her wedding. Nobody plays it twice in a row; the room needs recovery time.

Ballad is the right label because a ballad is a slow, sentimental song that tells a story — the trucker's calls unfold verse by verse like chapters. An anthem lifts a crowd and a jingle sells tires, but neither carries characters through time the way a ballad does.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

lament: a grief-song — the story falls away and only the mourning is left

serenade: sung to one listener, courting rather than storytelling

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

anthem: a rousing, chest-out crowd song — the opposite mood

ditty: a scrap of throwaway song with no story in it

Where it sits · how much emotional weight the song carries — jingle → ballad → lament

jingle vs. ballad: A jingle is the featherweight of song — thirty catchy seconds built to sell something, with nothing at stake.

lament vs. ballad: A lament goes further than a ballad — the ballad's story gives way entirely to grieving, sung sorrow with no plot left.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — ball

Root — ball: to dance (Late Latin ballare)

Suffix — -ad

Suffix — -ad: noun ending (worn down from Provençal -ada)

Put it together

Put it together: Ball (to dance) + -ad (noun ending) = 'a dancing song.' In old Provence a balada was sung while the village danced; over the centuries the dance dropped away, and the story and the feeling stayed. The same ballare also gives English the dancing kind of ball, as in a masked ball.

Use the root in a new word: ballet

Use the root in a new word: ballet: Ballet keeps the root's original meaning on stage: dance made into an art of its own.

Word Choice

neutral / musical

Ballad names a kind of song, not just any slow tune: there should be a story with people in it and feeling in the telling. For a crowd-rouser, anthem; for a baby, lullaby; for grief with no plot, lament.
